title: The spots your toothbrush misses

topic.title: The spots your toothbrush misses
topic.question: Which spots do people miss when brushing?

scenes.text: Your toothbrush skips one spot every morning.
Start at the gumline, not the center of the tooth.

scenes.caption: Angle the brush toward the gumline.

scenes.text: Two minutes gives each area enough attention.
Ask if your brushing angle looks right at your next checkup.

voiceover.text: Ever feel like your brush misses the same spot every morning? Start where the tooth meets the gums, not the middle. Tilt a soft brush toward that edge. Skip the fast scrubbing. Use small, gentle strokes instead. Common misses are back molars, inside front teeth, and along the gums. About two minutes gives each area enough attention. At your next checkup, ask us to look at your brushing angle.

copy.caption: Your toothbrush skips the same spots every morning: back molars, the inside of your front teeth and along the gums. Angle a soft brush toward the gumline and use small, gentle strokes for about two minutes. Ask us to check your brushing angle at your next visit.

shoot_card.opening: Today: the three spots most people miss when they brush.
points: Start where the tooth meets the gum, not the middle of the tooth.
Small, gentle strokes clean better than fast scrubbing.
Back molars, the inside of the front teeth and the gumline are the usual misses.
shoot_card.closing: At your next check-up, ask us to look at your brushing angle.

Pick a quiet room so your voice is clear.

title: Does whitening thin your enamel?

scenes.text: Whitening your teeth? Not as harsh as you think.
Whitening done as directed usually doesn't thin enamel.
Ask your dentist which whitening plan fits your teeth.

voiceover.text: Thinking about whitening because it might wear down enamel? Usually, when you use it the way your dentist tells you, it doesn’t thin enamel. It works on stains, not tooth structure. What you’re more likely to notice is some short-term sensitivity, and that usually fades. Afterward, skip dark drinks and follow your dentist’s advice to find the right plan for your teeth.

copy.caption: Worried whitening will wear down your enamel? Used as your dentist directs, whitening works on stains, not tooth structure. Short-lived sensitivity is the more common side effect, and it usually fades. Ask us which whitening plan fits your teeth.

shoot_card.opening: A question I hear a lot: does whitening thin your enamel?
points: Whitening done as directed works on stains, not on the enamel itself.
Some sensitivity for a few days is common and usually fades.
Skip dark drinks right after whitening and follow the plan you were given.
shoot_card.closing: If you are thinking about whitening, ask us which plan fits your teeth.

title: Keeping clear aligners fresh

topic.title: Keeping clear aligners fresh
topic.question: How should I clean my clear aligners?

scenes.text: Rinse them every time you take them out.
Brush them gently so buildup doesn't linger.
Use cool water so the tray keeps its shape.
Ask if your aligner care routine needs a quick check.

voiceover.text: Do your aligners start smelling off by evening? Rinse them each time you take them out, then put them away clean. Use a soft brush with cool water, and skip toothpaste. Brush gently so buildup doesn’t hang around. Cool water helps the tray keep its shape. If you want, ask us to check your routine.

copy.caption: Aligners smelling off by evening? Rinse them every time you take them out, brush them gently with a soft brush and cool water, and skip toothpaste. Cool water helps the trays keep their shape. Ask us if your aligner routine needs a quick check.

shoot_card.opening: Three habits that keep clear aligners fresh all day.
points: Rinse the trays every time you take them out.
Brush them gently with a soft brush and cool water, without toothpaste.
Hot water can warp the trays, so keep it cool.
shoot_card.closing: Bring your aligners to your next visit and we will check your routine.
